t: For necessary expenses for countering potential biological, disease, and chemical threats to civilian populations, $33,885,000: Provided, That the total amount appropriated and, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the functions, personnel, assets, and liabilities of the National Disaster Medical System established under section 2811(b) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 300hh–11(b)), including any functions of the Secretary of Homeland Security relating to such System, shall be permanently transferred to the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services effective January 1, 2007.

fable.w: This section appropriates funds and transfers the National Disaster Medical System from the Secretary of Homeland Security to the Secretary of Health and Human Services, which is a reorganization entirely inside the federal government. The tempting reading is that the reference to threats to "civilian populations" or a transfer between departments implies coordination with outsiders, but no state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, given a hearing, or granted a right to sue. No rulemaking or comment process is required either.
fable.s: shall be permanently transferred to the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services effective January 1, 2007

opus.w: This section provides funding and moves a program from one federal department to another. Both the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Health and Human Services are inside the federal government, so this is intra-government reorganization, not participation. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, placed on an advisory body, or granted a right to sue.
opus.s: the functions, personnel, assets, and liabilities of the National Disaster Medical System established under section 2811(b) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 300hh–11(b)), including any functions of the Secretary of Homeland Security relating to such System, shall be permanently transferred to the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services
opus.b: 1. **The tempting reading:** the section moves the National Disaster Medical System from the Secretary of Homeland Security to the Secretary of Health and Human Services, which sounds like coordination. It isn't participation, because both sides of the transfer are inside the federal government. Nothing here brings in states, experts, the public or any other outside party, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. The rest of the section is just an appropriation.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates the transfer of functions, personnel, and assets from the Department of Homeland Security to the Department of Health and Human Services. Both entities are part of the federal government. The definition of participation requires interaction with parties outside the federal government (e.g., states, public, experts). Intra-agency transfers do not constitute participation.
qwen_chat.s: the functions, personnel, assets, and liabilities of the National Disaster Medical System established under section 2811(b) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 300hh–11(b)), including any functions of the Secretary of Homeland Security relating to such System, shall be permanently transferred to the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that transferring functions to the Secretary of HHS involves coordination with the Secretary of Homeland Security, implying participation. However, this is an intra-governmental transfer of authority and assets between federal agencies. Both the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of HHS are inside the federal government. There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities required for this transfer.
